card.name: Tari Piring (Plate dance)
card.era: Pre-Islamic harvest ritual origins; popularized by Huriah Adam
card.tagline: Minangkabau plate dance of whirling balanced plates
card.profile: Tari Piring (Piriang) is a traditional Minangkabau plate dance from West Sumatra, traditionally from Solok (Wikipedia; Indonesia.travel). Performed by women, men or couples, each dancer holds a plate in each hand and vigorously rotates them in fast formations without dropping them, tapping the plates with a finger ring for sonic accompaniment. It originated as a harvest fertility ritual of gratitude to the gods, in which offerings of food were carried on plates; with the arrival of Islam it became a performance dance rather than worship. Movements draw on Minangkabau silat, and it is accompanied by the talempong and saluang. Performances often end with dancers stepping barefoot on broken plate shards.
card.insight: Now performed at weddings and welcomes alongside saman, pendet and jaipong, Tari Piring has become one of Indonesia's signature dances for promoting national tourism and culture (BINUS; Indonesia Sentinel).
